title: Removing Uniswap V3 liquidity requires the proxy to own the position NFT and validates the declared minimums against what was actually collected
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.9.3.3 opens with an ownership assertion: `require(positionManager.ownerOf(tokenId) == address(proxy), "UniswapV3Lib/proxy-does-not-own-token-id")`, alongside snapshots of the proxy's `token0` and `token1` balances. Because a Uniswap V3 position is an NFT identified by an arbitrary integer, without this check a relayer could pass any `tokenId` and have the controller operate on a stranger's position.

The more unusual step is A...9.3.6, run *after* `decreaseLiquidity` and `collect`:

```
require(params.min.amount0 >= (amount0CollectedAfter - amount0CollectedBefore) * params.maxSlippage / 1e18, "UniswapV3Lib/min-amount-below-bound");
```

The comparison runs in the direction that constrains the **caller's declaration**, not the execution: the minimum the relayer supplied must be at least the realised amount scaled by `maxSlippage`. A relayer who declared a comfortably low minimum — the usual way to guarantee a fill — reverts, even though the withdrawal itself came out fine.

That is the same "constraint on the constraint" idea used pre-emptively on Curve (A...8.1.4), applied here after the fact because the realised amount is only knowable post-collection. Its effect is to force relayers to submit tight, well-estimated minimums as a matter of routine, so the `min` values passed to the position manager are genuinely protective rather than nominal.

Rate limits are then decreased per token and only when non-zero (A...9.3.7), keyed by token-and-pool, keeping the withdraw budget separate per side of the pool.
description: ownerOf must equal the proxy, and afterwards each declared min must be at least the measured collected delta scaled by maxSlippage — so a slack declaration reverts a successful execution.
